01 / READOUT

Summary

There is a visible market for short recreational workshops, cultural food experiences, and structured culinary training. Cook & Bake spans all three, but its longer courses need clearer proof of depth and outcomes to support premium fees.

Positioning

Three levels of commitment

Entry workshops at S$160–220; specialist short courses at S$360–760; advanced multi-week programmes at S$980–1,580. Prices are proposed fees from the supplied course catalogue.

Opportunity

Room between trial and training

Examples in the market range from community workshops to longer institute programmes. Show total contact hours, what students take home, materials, and instructor credentials so customers can judge the premium.

Evidence gap

Validate conversion early

Published competitor prices are not directly comparable: durations, subsidy eligibility, ingredients, and class formats differ. Booking/search volumes, market size, and our own willingness-to-pay are UNKNOWN.

02 / CUSTOMER HYPOTHESES

Personas

Three practical hypotheses for launch messaging and customer interviews. These are not measured market segments; segment sizes and willingness-to-pay are UNKNOWN.

01 · Skill builder

The ambitious home cook

Wants repeatable technique and confidence: bread, pastry, knife skills, or a cuisine learned from scratch. Likely values small groups, hands-on practice, useful take-home results, and a clear progression.

Offer examples: ITE culinary short courses, ACI Bread Making 1, and Bake King’s classes. Sources dated 16 Sep 2026 or accessed 24 Sep 2026.

02 · Experience seeker

The pair or visitor planning an outing

Books a social activity with a story to tell: local food, regional cuisine, or a shared cooking session. Convenience, a memorable meal, and easy booking may matter more than a certificate.

Offer examples: Food Playground’s cultural cooking class and Let’s Go Cook’s cuisine classes. Accessed 24 Sep 2026.

03 · Accessible learner / gift buyer

The cautious first-timer

Needs a manageable first step: a one-session workshop, beginner-friendly instruction, or a giftable class with a clear duration and finished product. Price transparency and suitability information reduce friction.

Offer examples: ABC Cooking Studio trial classes and OnePA adult workshops. Accessed 24 Sep 2026.

05 / DEMAND CONTEXT

Demand and seasonality

Signals support testing culinary experiences, not a forecast of course bookings. No public source reviewed provides Singapore cooking-class search volume, market size, or competitor occupancy; those figures are UNKNOWN.

S$23.9bSingapore tourism receipts in the first three quarters of 2025, up 6.5% year-on-year. This is a broad visitor-spending signal, not cooking-class revenue.

Singapore Tourism Board · 3 Feb 2026

17–18mVisitor arrivals forecast for 2026 by STB. This may support testing visitor-friendly cultural classes; addressable class demand is UNKNOWN.

Singapore Tourism Board · 3 Feb 2026

Seasonal hooksFood event programming included GastroBeats (5–28 Jun 2026) and Sentosa GrillFest (23 Jul–16 Aug 2026); use event-timed menus and campaign tests, not assumed uplift.

GastroBeats · 2026 · Sentosa · 18 Jun 2026

Seasonality read: Food festivals create timely themes in mid-year; baking and gifting offers can be tested around year-end. The supplied catalogue lists October and December 2026 intakes, but those dates alone do not establish seasonal demand. Booking trends, search interest, festival conversion, and school-holiday impact are UNKNOWN.
06 / FIRST COHORTS

The five to launch first

A portfolio test across accessible entry points, distinctive baking skills, and a culturally relevant cooking experience. These are strategic hypotheses based on catalog fit and visible market references, not a demand ranking.

01

Knife Skills & Kitchen Essentials

S$160 · one week listed · Bukit Timah. Lowest proposed price and a broadly useful beginner skill make this the clearest first-booking test. It can introduce the academy without asking for a multi-week commitment.

S$160
02

Cookie & Biscuit Baking

S$180 · one week listed · Orchard Road. Beginner-friendly, giftable take-home output with a low total ticket; listed near ITE short-course examples, though inclusions differ.

S$180
03

Macaron Masterclass

S$420 · two weeks listed · Orchard Road. A specialist, visually demonstrable bakery skill that can test demand beyond introductory workshops and create strong shareable results.

S$420
04

Thai Street Food Cooking

S$540 · three weeks listed · Bukit Timah. A recognizable cuisine with a hands-on social angle; test whether customers pay for repeat instruction beyond shorter experience classes.

S$540
05

Artisan Sourdough Bread Baking

S$680 · four weeks listed · Orchard Road. Strong skill progression and take-home practice distinguish it from one-off workshops; ACI’s S$970 bread programme shows a higher published training reference, not direct equivalence.

S$680

Sources, dates & method

Research checked: 24 September 2026. Competitor prices and pages are linked inline and dated where the source provides a date; “accessed” indicates the review date. Prices may change. The 20 proposed fees, campus assignments, course lengths in weeks, intake dates, and class size come from the user-provided course catalogue (courses.json); treated as proposal inputs, not independently verified market facts.

Comparability: Published examples differ in number of lessons, contact hours, subsidy status, class format, and included ingredients. Course meeting counts, per-session equivalence, booking volume, demand forecasts for these classes, and willingness-to-pay: UNKNOWN. Personas and launch order are strategic hypotheses for validation through first-cohort conversion and customer interviews.

Useful checks before opening registration: verify live prices and dates; state exact meeting count and contact hours; confirm what is included; interview prospective learners; track page-to-booking conversion and seat fill by course and intake.
